sources.title: Controlled Language for Multilingual Document Production: Experience with Caterpillar Technical English
sources.author: Christine Kamprath, Eric Adolphson, Teruko Mitamura, Eric Nyberg
sources.accessScope: Author-uploaded full-text sections 1–4, as recorded in initial research; historical report, not internal manual or current standard. Publication PDF located at https://aclanthology.org/www.mt-archive.info/90/CLAW-1998-Kamprath.pdf .
sources.rights: No permissive paper, dictionary, or tool license established; no source text or controlled vocabulary bundled.

rules.intent: Preserve facts, numbers, units, negation, conditions, exceptions, uncertainty, quotations, citations, and code; distinguish supplied evidence from inference.
rules.rationale: Project-wide meaning-preservation requirement; style never authorizes a factual change.

rules.intent: Use the supplied project glossary and intended domain senses consistently; flag missing or conflicting terms.
rules.rationale: Adapts documented terminology control without inventing Caterpillar's dictionary.
exceptions: A domain may explicitly approve more than one sense; distinguish the sense in context rather than imposing one-word-one-meaning absolutely.

rules.intent: Resolve unclear references, attachment, omitted participants, and word senses that could change the translation or action.
rules.rationale: Adapts documented disambiguation for source authoring.
exceptions: If the source does not identify the intended actor or sense, ask a targeted question or flag it; never guess silently.

rules.intent: Keep procedural sequence, conditions, warnings, markup, and necessary grammatical complexity intact while clarifying English.
rules.rationale: Adapts CTE's translation-oriented approach rather than substituting CFE's vocabulary restriction.
exceptions: A longer conditional construction may be necessary to preserve the technical relationship.

rules.intent: Use consistent wording for genuinely equivalent information and review unresolved glossary/grammar decisions before claiming translation readiness.
rules.rationale: Adapts reusable information elements and interactive review; no proprietary checker is reproduced.
exceptions: Similar-looking instructions with different conditions must remain distinct; without a supplied grammar only general principles can be checked.
